name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information 
system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows 
citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions 
found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the 
streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: 
https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source 
software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS 
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, 
and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. 
The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through 
that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin 
(which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the 
following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is 
also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its 
file path on the server). The possible problem categories are: 
• Waterworks – Drinking water 
• Architectural Barriers 
• Sewerage 
• Public Lighting 
• Waste 
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights 
• Roads and Urban Furniture 
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds 
• Other 
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want 
the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).  

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE 
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the 
Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted 
or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, 
Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which 
point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once 
the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue 
resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be 
set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the 
technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation 
from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).  
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for 
example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), 
two cases are possible: - Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the 
report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the 
report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance 
workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to 
the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer 
can mark the report as resolved. 
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company 
(bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if 
previously configured by the municipal administrator. - Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company 
updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff 
member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state. 


C. CITIZEN UPDATES 
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding 
their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a 
notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators 
updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can 
reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each 
time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be 
disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). 
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the 
Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the 
citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by 
category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was 
chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.  
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into 
Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the 
same rules as for their own reports). 


D. STATISTICS 
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated 
section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, 
or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to 
administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

highLevelGoals: Citizens should be able to submit detailed reports about urban problems, including location, description, category, and supporting photos, to the public administration.
Citizens should receive notifications and emails regarding status changes and messages related to their submitted reports, fostering trust and transparency.
Citizens should have the option to submit reports anonymously, protecting their privacy while still contributing to urban improvement.
Citizens should be able to track the progress and status of other citizens' public reports, promoting community awareness and engagement.
Organization Office Staff should be able to efficiently review, accept, or reject citizen reports to ensure their validity and appropriateness for further processing.
Organization Office Staff must provide mandatory written explanations for rejected reports to maintain transparency and citizen trust.
Technical Office Staff should be able to track and update the status of accepted reports through various stages, from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved', ensuring efficient issue resolution.
Technical Office Staff should be able to assign accepted reports to the appropriate internal technical offices or external maintenance companies based on the problem category.
Technical Office Staff should be able to exchange private comments and information with external maintenance personnel regarding specific reports.
External Maintenance Workers should be able to access reports assigned to them, update their status, and mark them as resolved upon completion of work.
External Maintenance Workers should be able to exchange private information and comments with the Technical Office Staff regarding the progress of assigned reports.
The Municipal Administrator should be able to configure the system to automatically assign reports of certain categories to external companies, streamlining the workflow.
The Municipal Administrator should be able to view detailed private statistics, including charts and tables, to monitor system performance and identify trends.
Public Viewers should be able to view accepted reports on an interactive map and in a summary table, promoting transparency and public awareness of urban problems.
Public Viewers should be able to access public statistics, such as the number of reports per category and trends over time, to understand the overall state of urban environment management.
lowLevelGoals: Allow the citizen to create a new user account by providing a username, first name, last name, and email address.
Allow the citizen to confirm their email address by clicking a link received via email to activate their account.
Allow the citizen to log into their existing account using their registered email and password.
Allow the citizen to choose a predefined category for the urban inconvenience from a list provided by the system.
Allow the citizen to input a detailed textual description of the urban inconvenience.
Allow the citizen to select a point on a map to specify the location of the urban inconvenience, capturing its latitude and longitude.
Allow the citizen to upload up to three mandatory image files to be attached as supporting evidence to the report.
Allow the citizen to choose whether to submit the urban inconvenience report anonymously or with their identity.
Allow the citizen to finalize and send the compiled report (including category, description, location, photos, and anonymity status) to the public administration.
Allow the citizen to view a list of all urban inconvenience reports they have previously submitted.
Allow the citizen to access and view the full details, including current status, of a specific submitted report.
Allow the citizen to receive automated notifications when the processing status of one of their submitted reports changes.
Allow the citizen to view messages sent by municipal operators regarding their submitted reports.
Allow the citizen to send a reply message to a municipal operator regarding a specific submitted report.
The system shall send a push notification to the citizen's registered device when the status of their submitted report is updated.

The system shall send an email to the citizen's registered email address when the status of their submitted report is updated, provided the citizen has not disabled email notifications in their settings.
The system shall send a push notification to the citizen's registered device when a new message or comment is added to their submitted report.

The system shall send an email to the citizen's registered email address when a new message or comment is added to their submitted report, provided the citizen has not disabled email notifications in their settings.
The system shall display an in-app notification to the citizen within the application when the status of their submitted report is updated.
The system shall display an in-app notification to the citizen within the application when a new message or comment is added to their submitted report.
The system shall allow the citizen to compose and send a reply to a message received from a municipal operator regarding their report.
The system shall allow the citizen to retrieve a paginated list of all reports they have submitted, including their current status.
The system shall allow the citizen to retrieve the full details, status history, and associated messages for a specific report they have submitted.
The system shall allow the citizen to retrieve a paginated list of all publicly visible reports on the Participium portal.
The system shall allow the citizen to filter the list of public reports by a specified category.
The system shall allow the citizen to filter the list of public reports by a specified status.
The system shall allow the citizen to filter the list of public reports by a specified date range (e.g., submission date).
The system shall allow the citizen to sort the list of public reports by category in ascending or descending order.
The system shall allow the citizen to sort the list of public reports by status in ascending or descending order.
The system shall allow the citizen to sort the list of public reports by submission date in ascending or descending order.
The system shall allow the citizen to retrieve the full details and current status for any publicly visible report.
The system shall allow the citizen to register to follow a specific public report to receive updates.
The system shall allow the citizen to deregister from following a specific public report.
The system shall send a push notification to the citizen's registered device when the status of a report they are following is updated.
The system shall send an email to the citizen's registered email address when the status of a report they are following is updated, provided email notifications are enabled.
The system shall send a push notification to the citizen's registered device when a new message or comment is added to a report they are following.
The system shall send an email to the citizen's registered email address when a new message or comment is added to a report they are following, provided email notifications are enabled.

A citizen must be able to explicitly set a boolean flag during the report submission process to indicate whether the new urban inconvenience report should be submitted anonymously or with their registered identity attached.
The system shall allow a Citizen to request and receive a paginated list of all public reports, including basic information like ID, title, status, and submission date, to browse available reports.
The system shall allow a Citizen to filter the displayed list of public reports based on their current status (e.g., 'Pending', 'In Progress', 'Resolved') to narrow down relevant reports.
The system shall allow a Citizen to search for public reports using keywords present in their title or description to find specific reports of interest.

The system shall allow a Citizen to request and receive comprehensive details for a selected public report, including its full description, location, attached media, and a history of status updates, to understand its context.
The system shall allow a Citizen to register their interest in a specific public report to receive automatic notifications when its status changes, enabling them to 'follow' its progress.
The system shall allow a Citizen to revoke their subscription to status updates for a specific public report, ceasing to receive further notifications.
The system shall allow a Citizen to request and receive a list of all public reports they are currently subscribed to for updates, providing an overview of their followed items.
The system shall automatically send a notification (e.g., push notification, email) to a Citizen when the status of a public report they are subscribed to changes, informing them of the update.
The system shall allow a Citizen to request and view a list of all status update notifications received for public reports they are subscribed to, providing an overview of recent changes and updates.
The system shall allow the Organization Office Staff to retrieve a paginated list of all citizen reports currently awaiting preliminary review, including their basic status and submission date.

The system shall allow the Organization Office Staff to retrieve and display all detailed information for a specific citizen report, identified by its unique ID, including reporter details, location, and description.
The system shall allow the Organization Office Staff to retrieve and view any media files (e.g., images, videos) attached to a specific citizen report to aid in the review process.

The system shall allow the Organization Office Staff to update the status of a specific citizen report to 'In Progress' and optionally add a review comment, marking it as accepted for further processing.

The system shall allow the Organization Office Staff to update the status of a specific citizen report to 'Rejected' and provide a mandatory reason for rejection, indicating it is not suitable for further processing.
The Organization Office Staff must be able to query and retrieve the full details of a specific citizen report by its unique identifier to assess its validity for approval or rejection.

The Organization Office Staff must be able to select a citizen report and trigger the system's rejection workflow, which prompts for a mandatory explanation and sets the report to a 'pending rejection explanation' state.

The Organization Office Staff must be able to submit a detailed textual explanation for a specific report's rejection, which the system will store and associate with the report as the mandatory justification.

The Organization Office Staff must be able to finalize the rejection of a citizen report, ensuring that the previously recorded mandatory explanation is securely attached, the report status is updated to 'Rejected', and the citizen is notified.
The Citizen must be able to create a new user account by providing necessary personal information.
The Citizen must be able to confirm their email address via a system-sent link to activate their account.
The Citizen must be able to submit a new report, including a description, location (map), and optional photos.
The Citizen must be able to select whether their submitted report is anonymous or linked to their identity.
The Organization Office Staff must be able to view a list of all citizen reports awaiting initial review.
The Organization Office Staff must be able to select a citizen report and mark it as 'Approved', making it available for assignment.
The Organization Office Staff must be able to assign an approved report to a specific Technical Office.
The Technical Office Staff must be able to view a list of reports assigned to their specific office.
The Technical Office Staff must be able to change the status of an assigned report to 'In Progress'.
The Technical Office Staff must be able to change the status of an assigned report to 'Work in Progress' when external work is initiated.
The Technical Office Staff must be able to change the status of an assigned report to 'Suspended' with a mandatory reason.
The Technical Office Staff must be able to mark an assigned report as 'Resolved', indicating completion.
The External Maintenance Personnel must be able to view a list of reports assigned to their company.
The External Maintenance Personnel must be able to update the status of a report they are working on (e.g., 'Work in Progress', 'Completed').
The External Maintenance Personnel must be able to add comments or notes to an assigned report.
The System must be able to send an email or in-platform notification to a citizen when their report's status changes.
The System must be able to send a notification to Technical Office Staff when a new report is assigned to their office.
The Administrator must be able to trigger the generation of public statistics regarding report types and resolution rates.
The Administrator must be able to trigger the generation of private, detailed statistics for internal analysis.
The Administrator must be able to view all reports geographically on an interactive map interface.
The Administrator must be able to view all reports in a sortable and filterable table format.
The Technical Office Staff should be able to fetch a list of all reports that have been accepted by the system, regardless of their current resolution stage.
The Technical Office Staff should be able to view all detailed information for a particular accepted report by its unique identifier.

The Technical Office Staff should be able to retrieve a subset of accepted reports based on their current status (e.g., 'Pending Approval', 'In Progress', 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', 'Resolved').
The Technical Office Staff should be able to assign an accepted report to a specific external company for resolution, updating its status accordingly.
The Technical Office Staff should be able to assign an accepted report to a specific internal technician or a designated internal team for resolution, updating its status accordingly.
The Technical Office Staff should be able to change the status of an assigned report to 'Work in Progress' once intervention is planned.
The Technical Office Staff should be able to change the status of an active report to 'Suspended' if work needs to be temporarily halted.
The Technical Office Staff should be able to mark a report as 'Resolved' on behalf of an external company that does not have direct system access, after verifying its completion.
The Technical Office Staff should be able to mark a report as 'Resolved' after its resolution has been verified and confirmed, for cases not involving manual resolution for external companies.

The Technical Office Staff should be able to append textual comments or notes to any accepted report, visible only to internal staff and assigned external maintenance workers, to document progress, issues, or other relevant information.

The system shall allow the Technical Office Staff to query and retrieve a list of all reports that are in the 'In Progress' state and have not yet been assigned to a responsible party, typically via an API call like GET /api/reports?status=in_progress&assigned=false.

The system shall allow the Technical Office Staff to retrieve the full details of a selected 'In Progress' report, including its problem category, description, and location, to inform the assignment decision, typically via an API call like GET /api/reports/{reportId}.

The system shall allow the Technical Office Staff to query and retrieve a list of internal technical offices or external maintenance companies, potentially filtered by problem category or expertise, that are eligible to be assigned a report, typically via an API call like GET /api/responsibleParties?category={problemCategory}.

The system shall allow the Technical Office Staff to retrieve a list of individual users (staff members or external personnel) associated with a selected internal technical office or external maintenance company, to facilitate specific user assignment, typically via an API call like GET /api/responsibleParties/{partyId}/users.

The system shall allow the Technical Office Staff to update a specific 'In Progress' report by associating it with a selected individual user from an internal technical office or external maintenance company, typically via an API call like PUT /api/reports/{reportId}/assignment with a payload containing the assigned user ID.

The system shall allow the Technical Office Staff to add a comment or note to an assigned report, intended for the assigned user, to provide additional instructions or context, typically via an API call like POST /api/reports/{reportId}/comments with a payload containing the comment text.

The system shall allow the Technical Office Staff to update the status of an assigned report from 'In Progress' to 'Work in Progress' after planning the intervention and assigning it to a specific user, indicating it's ready for the assigned party to commence work, typically via an API call like PATCH /api/reports/{reportId}/status with a payload containing the new status 'work_in_progress'.

The Technical Office Staff shall be able to submit a new private textual comment, associating it with a specific report identified by its unique ID, to facilitate direct communication with external maintenance personnel regarding that report.

The Technical Office Staff shall be able to request and view the complete chronological list of private comments, including those from external maintenance personnel, associated with a given report ID, to review past communications.

The Technical Office Staff shall be able to assign an accepted report, identified by its unique ID, to a specific internal technical office or an external maintenance personnel group, thereby communicating responsibility for its resolution.

The Technical Office Staff shall be able to update the status of a report, identified by its unique ID, to reflect its current stage in the resolution lifecycle (e.g., 'In Progress', 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', 'Resolved'), thereby communicating its progress to relevant parties.

The Technical Office Staff shall be able to manually mark a report, identified by its unique ID, as 'Closed' when it has been resolved by an external company operating outside the system, thereby communicating its final resolution status.
The system shall allow an External Maintenance Worker to authenticate using their credentials to gain access to the system's functionalities.
The system shall allow an authenticated External Maintenance Worker to retrieve a list of all reports currently assigned to them.
The system shall allow an authenticated External Maintenance Worker to view the detailed information of a specific report assigned to them, identified by its unique ID.
The system shall allow an authenticated External Maintenance Worker to retrieve and view all existing comments and information exchanged on a specific assigned report.
The system shall allow an authenticated External Maintenance Worker to add a new comment or piece of information to a specific assigned report, facilitating communication with the technical office.
The system shall allow an authenticated External Maintenance Worker to update the status of an assigned report to 'In Progress'.
The system shall allow an authenticated External Maintenance Worker to mark an assigned report as 'Resolved' upon completion of work.
The system shall allow an authenticated External Maintenance Worker to add descriptive notes or details when marking a report as 'Resolved'.

The External Maintenance Worker should be able to send a request to the system to retrieve and display all existing text-based comments and messages associated with a particular urban issue report, including those from Technical Office Staff.
The External Maintenance Worker should be able to send a new text-based comment or message to the system, associating it with a specific urban issue report, for the Technical Office Staff to review.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to fetch a list of all predefined or custom report categories that can be used for automatic assignment.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to fetch a list of all registered external companies that can receive automatic report assignments.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to define a new rule that automatically assigns reports of a specified category to a designated external company.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to modify an existing automatic assignment rule, such as changing the assigned company or the report category.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to enable a previously defined automatic assignment rule, making it active for incoming reports.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to disable an active automatic assignment rule, preventing it from being applied to new reports.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to remove an automatic assignment rule entirely from the system.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to retrieve a list of all currently configured automatic assignment rules, including their status, categories, and assigned companies.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to authenticate their credentials to gain access to private system statistics.
The system should provide a list of available private system statistic types (e.g., 'Reports by Category', 'Report Trends') that the Municipal Administrator can view.
The system should retrieve raw data showing the number of reports for each category within a specified time range (e.g., 'last 7 days', 'custom date range') for the Municipal Administrator.
The system should retrieve raw data showing report trends over a specified period (day, week, or month) within a defined time range for the Municipal Administrator.
The system should render a graphical chart (e.g., bar chart) based on the requested 'Reports by Category' data for the Municipal Administrator.
The system should display a tabular representation of the requested 'Reports by Category' data for the Municipal Administrator.
The system should render a graphical chart (e.g., line chart) based on the requested 'Report Trend' data for the Municipal Administrator.
The system should display a tabular representation of the requested 'Report Trend' data for the Municipal Administrator.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to view the currently configured automatic assignment rules, including associated problem categories and external companies.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to specify an external company to which reports of a particular problem category should be automatically assigned.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to change the external company assigned to a specific problem category for automatic assignments.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to remove an automatic assignment rule for a specific problem category.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to activate the automatic assignment feature for all configured rules.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to deactivate the automatic assignment feature, preventing any new automatic assignments.
The system should allow the Municipal Administrator to view whether the automatic assignment feature is currently enabled or disabled.

The system should allow a Public Viewer to request and receive a list of all currently accepted urban issue reports, including their geographical coordinates and basic identifying information, suitable for rendering as markers on an interactive map.

The system should allow a Public Viewer to apply filters (e.g., issue type, date range, status) to the displayed accepted urban issue reports on the map, and receive an updated list of reports matching the criteria.
The system should allow a Public Viewer to select a specific report marker on the map and request its full details (e.g., full description, images, exact location, resolution status) for display.

The system should allow a Public Viewer to request and receive a paginated list of accepted urban issue reports, including key summary attributes (e.g., report ID, issue type, submission date, general location, current status) for display in a summary table.

The system should allow a Public Viewer to apply filters (e.g., issue type, date range, keyword search, status) to the list of accepted urban issue reports in the summary table, and receive an updated paginated list of reports matching the criteria.

The system should allow a Public Viewer to sort the paginated list of accepted urban issue reports in the summary table by any of the displayed attributes (e.g., submission date, issue type, status) in ascending or descending order.

The system should allow a Public Viewer to select a specific report row in the summary table and request its full details (e.g., full description, images, exact location, resolution status) for display.
The system should allow a Public Viewer to request and receive aggregated public statistics, such as the total number of accepted reports, total resolved reports, and overall resolution rate.
The system should allow a Public Viewer to request and receive public statistics broken down by urban issue category, showing the count of accepted reports for each category.
The system should allow a Public Viewer to request and receive public statistics showing trends of accepted urban issue reports over specified time periods (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly counts).
The system shall allow a Public Viewer to retrieve the total number of all urban issue reports recorded in the system.
The system shall allow a Public Viewer to retrieve a list of urban issue categories along with the count of reports for each category.
The system shall allow a Public Viewer to retrieve time-series data showing the number of urban issue reports submitted over a specified period (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly).

baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are comprehensive, accurate, and well-aligned with the software description. They correctly cover the functional requirements for all identified actors (Citizens, Organization Office, Technical Office, External Workers, Administrators, and Public Viewers). The goals appropriately abstract the 'why' and 'what' of the system (e.g., enabling reporting, managing lifecycle, ensuring transparency) without diving into low-level technical implementation details. There are no contradictions or significant omissions regarding the functional scope described in the text.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals:
[Citizen -> Enable citizens to report urban inconveniences] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a minor contradiction. 
1. **Contradiction**: The goal `UploadReportPhoto` states that the citizen must upload "up to three mandatory image files". The description explicitly states "It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report)". Therefore, the goal should reflect that at least one photo is mandatory, not that all three are mandatory.
2. **Omissions**: Several functional capabilities described in the software description are missing from the low-level goals:
   - **Viewing Public Reports**: The description states that "Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table" and citizens can view the portal. There is no goal for viewing the public map or the public summary table of reports.
   - **Following Other Citizens' Reports**: The description mentions citizens can "follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications". There are no goals for following/unfollowing reports or receiving notifications for followed reports.
   - **User Settings**: The description mentions a "user settings panel" where users can disable email notifications and upload a personal photo. There are no goals for managing these settings.
   - **Viewing Statistics**: The description mentions public statistics are visible to non-registered users and citizens. There is no goal for viewing public statistics.

[Citizen -> Provide citizens with updates on their reports] Major omission and misalignment. The provided low-level goals only address the "Citizen Updates" aspect (notifications, viewing public reports, following reports). They completely fail to address the core functionality of the system: **Report Submission** (selecting map point, filling form, attaching photos, choosing anonymity) and **User Registration** (sign up, email confirmation). Furthermore, the high-level goal provided is too narrow ("Provide citizens with updates"), which causes the low-level goals to be incomplete relative to the full software description. The low-level goals should include actions like "Register new account", "Confirm registration via email link", "Submit new report with location and photos", and "View personal report details". Additionally, some low-level goals (like filtering/sorting public reports) are arguably better suited under a "View Public Reports" high-level goal rather than "Provide updates", though they are functionally correct. The primary issue is the missing submission and registration workflows.

[Citizen -> Allow citizens to control report anonymity] Major omission. The provided low-level goals only address the anonymity feature, completely ignoring the core functionalities of the system described in the software description, such as user registration, report submission (including map selection, form filling, and photo attachment), report lifecycle management, and receiving updates/notifications. Additionally, the actors list is incomplete, missing critical actors like the Municipality Administrator, Technical Office, and External Maintenance Personnel, which are necessary to fully represent the system. The high-level goals are also severely limited, focusing only on anonymity rather than the broader objective of enabling citizen participation in urban management.

[Citizen -> Enable citizens to follow public reports] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a significant omission. The high-level goal is "Enable citizens to follow public reports," and the description explicitly states that citizens can "follow other citizens’ open reports." However, the low-level goals only cover browsing, filtering, searching, and viewing details of public reports. They completely miss the core functionality of *following* (subscribing to) a specific report, which is the primary action implied by the high-level goal. While there is a goal to "Subscribe to status updates," it is framed generically and does not explicitly link to the act of following a specific public report as a distinct user action separate from just viewing it. More critically, the system description mentions that citizens can receive updates on *their own* reports and *followed* reports, but the low-level goals do not distinguish between the two or provide a clear mechanism for a citizen to initiate the "follow" action on a report they did not submit. The current set of goals describes a read-only browsing experience rather than an interactive following experience. Additionally, the goal "Send status update notification" is a system action, not a user action, and should be framed as the system's responsibility triggered by the user's follow action, but the user's action to *initiate* the follow is missing or poorly defined.

[Organization Office Staff -> Facilitate preliminary review of citizen reports] Input text must contain Feedback: ... and a final Score: line.

[Organization Office Staff -> Ensure clear communication for rejected reports] The provided low-level goals are severely incomplete and contain significant errors. 
1. **Major Omissions**: The goals completely ignore the core functionality for the primary actor, the Citizen. While there are a few goals for registration and submission, they miss critical features: viewing the public map/table (available to non-registered users), filtering/sorting reports, following other citizens' reports, receiving in-platform notifications, replying to messages from municipal operators, and managing user settings (disabling emails, uploading photos). 
2. **Actor Mismatch**: The input lists only "Organization Office Staff" as an actor, yet the low-level goals reference "Citizen", "Technical Office Staff", "External Maintenance Personnel", "System", and "Administrator". This inconsistency makes the model invalid.
3. **Incorrect Attribution**: Goals like `DisplayReportsOnMap` and `DisplayReportsInTable` are assigned to the "Administrator", but the description states these views are available to all users (including non-registered ones) for public reports. 
4. **Missing Functional Goals**: There are no goals for the Technical Office to assign reports to external companies (Case 1), nor for the system to handle the "Suspended" state logic correctly (the description says it's for organizational/technical reasons, not necessarily requiring a mandatory reason in the UI, though the goal adds a constraint not explicitly in the text, which is minor compared to the omissions).
5. **Contradiction**: The high-level goals provided in the prompt are extremely limited (only one goal for Organization Office Staff), yet the low-level goals reference many other high-level goals that were not provided in the input context. This suggests the assistant hallucinated the high-level goals or the input was truncated, but based on the provided text, the low-level goals do not align with the provided high-level goals.

[Technical Office Staff -> Manage the lifecycle of accepted reports] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a logical contradiction. 
1. **Contradiction**: The goal "Filter accepted reports by status" includes "Pending Approval" in its description. However, the high-level goal is to manage the lifecycle of *accepted* reports, and the system description states that "Pending Approval" reports are handled by the Organization Office, not the Technical Office. The Technical Office only sees reports after they are accepted (moved to "In Progress"). Including "Pending Approval" in the filter for the Technical Office is incorrect.
2. **Omissions**: The description explicitly states that "Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report". While there is a goal to "Add an internal comment", there is no goal for the Technical Office Staff to *view* or *read* the comments/updates provided by external maintenance workers. This is a critical part of the interaction and lifecycle management.
3. **Omissions**: The description mentions that the Technical Office assigns reports to the "technical office responsible, based on the problem category". While there is a goal to assign to an internal technician, the specific logic of assignment based on category is not explicitly captured as a distinct functional requirement or constraint in the low-level goals, though it might be implied. More importantly, the ability to *view* the external worker's updates is missing.

[Technical Office Staff -> Assign reports to responsible parties] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a logical contradiction regarding the report lifecycle. 
1. **Contradiction/Logic Error**: The high-level goal is to "Assign reports to responsible parties." According to the description, reports are assigned *after* approval, moving from "Pending Approval" to "In Progress". However, the low-level goal "Retrieve Unassigned In Progress Reports" implies that reports are already in the "In Progress" state *before* assignment. This contradicts the workflow where assignment happens *at* the transition to "In Progress" or immediately after. The system should retrieve reports in "Pending Approval" (if auto-assignment is configured) or newly approved reports to assign them.
2. **Major Omissions**: The high-level goal description explicitly states that Technical Office Staff are responsible for "updating their resolution status." The provided low-level goals only cover the assignment phase and moving to "Work in Progress." They completely omit the critical actions of:
   - Updating the status to "Suspended".
   - Updating the status to "Resolved" (closing the report).
   - Handling the specific case where external companies do *not* have access (manual update by staff).
   - Exchanging comments with external maintenance personnel (only adding comments is listed, not viewing/receiving them, though this might be part of the interaction).
3. **Scope**: The goals are too narrowly focused on the assignment mechanism and miss the broader lifecycle management responsibilities defined in the actor description and high-level goal.

[Technical Office Staff -> Facilitate internal communication on reports] The low-level goals are incomplete and contain a logical error in goal association. 
1. **Missing Goals**: The actor "Technical Office Staff" has significant responsibilities described in the system description (Section B) that are not covered by the provided low-level goals. Specifically, the staff must:
   - Assign reports to the responsible technical office based on category (currently, the goal "Assign a report..." exists but is incorrectly associated with the communication high-level goal, and the specific logic of assigning to the *responsible office* vs *external personnel* is conflated).
   - Manually move reports to "Resolved" for external companies without system access (Case 2). While "Manually close a resolved report" exists, it is also incorrectly associated with the communication goal.
   - The high-level goal provided is only "Facilitate internal communication". However, the actor's primary role is managing the report lifecycle (assignment, status updates, closing). There is a missing high-level goal for "Manage report lifecycle and assignment" or similar, which would properly house the goals for assigning, updating status, and closing reports.
2. **Incorrect Association**: The goals "Assign a report...", "Update the lifecycle status...", and "Manually close..." are functional actions related to workflow management, not just "internal communication". Associating them solely with "Facilitate internal communication" is semantically incorrect. They should be associated with a goal related to managing the report workflow/lifecycle.
3. **Scope**: The prompt asks to critique the work on defining low-level end-user goals. The provided set only covers a subset of the actor's actions (communication and some lifecycle steps) but fails to provide a coherent structure where lifecycle management is distinct from communication.

[External Maintenance Worker -> Enable external personnel to manage assigned reports] The low-level goals are well-structured and correctly identify the functional actions available to the External Maintenance Worker (authentication, viewing assigned reports, commenting, updating status to 'In Progress', and marking as 'Resolved'). However, there is a minor omission regarding the visibility of comments. The description explicitly states that comments exchanged between the technical office and external maintenance workers are "not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens)". While the current goal "View Report Comments/Information Exchange" implies viewing the relevant comments, it does not explicitly enforce the constraint that these comments are restricted from public/citizen view, which is a key functional requirement for this actor's interaction. Additionally, the goal "Add Completion Notes to Resolved Report" is slightly redundant or ambiguous; the description says the worker "can mark the report as resolved", and while adding notes is a reasonable inference for "exchange information", it is not explicitly mandated as a separate step distinct from the resolution action in the text (unlike the mandatory written explanation for rejections by the Organization Office). The main issue is the lack of explicit handling for the restricted visibility of the communication channel in the low-level goals, which is a critical functional aspect of the system design for this actor.

[External Maintenance Worker -> Facilitate communication with technical office staff] Major omission. The provided low-level goals only address the communication aspect (reading and writing comments) for the External Maintenance Worker. However, the software description explicitly states that external maintenance personnel can "move the report from Assigned to In Progress" and "mark the report as resolved." These are critical functional actions defined in the system's lifecycle (Section B, Case 1) and are completely missing from the low-level goals. Additionally, the high-level goals provided are extremely narrow, focusing solely on communication, which fails to represent the full scope of the actor's capabilities (status management) as described in the text. To improve, add low-level goals for updating the report status to "In Progress" and "Resolved," and ensure the high-level goals reflect the broader objective of managing assigned interventions.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) are evaluated against the parent High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to report urban inconveniences' and the project documentation. 

1. **Relevance**: All LLGs are directly related to the citizen's interaction with the reporting system. 
   - llg_001 to llg_003 (Registration/Authentication) are prerequisites for submitting reports, as the documentation states citizens can submit reports only if registered. 
   - llg_004 to llg_009 cover the specific data entry and submission steps (Category, Description, Location, Photos, Anonymity, Submit) mandated by Section A. 
   - llg_010 to llg_014 cover the post-submission visibility and communication aspects. While Section C ('Citizen Updates') is a separate section in the documentation, the parent HLG description is broad ('Enable citizens to report...'), and the actor description includes 'receive updates on their status'. Therefore, viewing one's own reports (llg_010, llg_011) and receiving updates/messages (llg_012, llg_013, llg_014) are essential capabilities for the citizen to complete the lifecycle of their report within the scope of this actor's responsibilities. They are not unrelated to the parent HLG; they are the feedback loop of the reporting process.

2. **Duplication/Contradiction**: There are no clear duplications. Each LLG represents a distinct functional step or capability. There are no contradictions with the documentation. 

3. **Missing Capabilities**: The core reporting flow is fully covered. The 'missing' capabilities might be things like 'Edit Report' (not mentioned in docs) or 'Delete Report' (not mentioned), but these are not essential based on the provided text. The requirement for 'mandatory fields' is covered by the specific LLGs for each field. 

4. **Conservative Review**: The instructions state to mark as unsupported only if clearly duplicated, contradictory, unrelated, or different intention. None of the LLGs fall into these categories. llg_010-014 are fine-grained but necessary for the citizen to track their reports, which is part of the 'reporting' experience defined in the actor description. 

Therefore, all LLGs are kept.

high_level_goal.description: Citizens should be able to track the progress and status of other citizens' public reports, promoting community awareness and engagement.

actor.name: Citizen
actor.description: Individuals who register to report urban inconveniences and receive updates on their status.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to follow public reports'. 

1. **Relevance**: All LLGs are directly related to the parent HLG. 
   - llg_001 to llg_004 support the 'track progress and status' aspect by allowing browsing, filtering, searching, and viewing details of public reports. The documentation confirms that accepted reports are visible on the map and summary table, and clicking opens a page with description. 
   - llg_005 to llg_009 support the 'follow' aspect. The documentation explicitly states: 'Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens' open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).' This validates the need for subscribe/unsubscribe (llg_005, llg_006), listing followed reports (llg_007), sending notifications (llg_008), and viewing those notifications (llg_009).

2. **Consistency**: There are no contradictions with the documentation. The states mentioned in llg_002 ('Pending', 'In Progress', 'Resolved') are consistent with the lifecycle described (Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected, and implicitly Resolved/Closed). While 'Resolved' isn't explicitly named as a state in the text (it says 'closes the report' or 'manually move the report to the Resolved state' in Case 2), it is a valid terminal state implied by the workflow. 

3. **Duplication**: No LLGs are clearly duplicated. llg_001 (list all) and llg_007 (list followed) are distinct. llg_008 (send notification) and llg_009 (view notifications) are distinct system actions vs. user actions.

4. **Missing Capabilities**: The decomposition covers the essential capabilities for following reports: discovery (list/search/filter), detail view, subscription management, and notification handling. No essential capability is missing for this specific HLG.

Therefore, the LLGs are supported and should be kept.

high_level_goal.description: Organization Office Staff must provide mandatory written explanations for rejected reports to maintain transparency and citizen trust.

actor.name: Organization Office Staff
actor.description: Municipal personnel responsible for the preliminary review and approval or rejection of citizen reports.

evaluation.rationale: The parent HLG 'Ensure clear communication for rejected reports' specifically concerns the Organization Office Staff providing mandatory written explanations for rejected reports. The current list of LLGs contains a mix of relevant and irrelevant goals. LLGs llg_002, llg_003, and llg_004 are directly relevant to the rejection process and explanation. However, the list is heavily polluted with LLGs belonging to other actors (Citizen, Technical Office, External Maintenance, Administrator) or unrelated functional areas (Registration, Report Submission, Statistics, Map/Table views, General Status Updates). Specifically: llg_005-llg_008 belong to the Citizen actor and are unrelated to the Organization Office's rejection duties. llg_009-llg_011 relate to the approval/assignment workflow, which is a sibling process, not the rejection communication. llg_012-llg_019 belong to Technical/External staff. llg_020-llg_025 belong to System/Administrator or are generic notifications/statistics. While llg_001 (Retrieve Details) is a prerequisite, it is generic. The presence of ~20 unrelated LLGs makes the current decomposition misleading and unsupported for the specific HLG. A regeneration is required to isolate only the LLGs pertinent to the Organization Office Staff's rejection and explanation workflow.
evaluation.regeneration_feedback: Regenerate the LLGs to focus exclusively on the 'Organization Office Staff' actor and the 'Ensure clear communication for rejected reports' HLG. Remove all LLGs associated with Citizens, Technical Office Staff, External Maintenance Personnel, and Administrators. Remove LLGs related to report submission, registration, approval, assignment, statistics, and general map/table viewing. The new set should strictly cover: 1) Identifying/Selecting a report for rejection, 2) Composing/Recording the mandatory written explanation, 3) Finalizing the rejection status, and 4) Ensuring the explanation is attached/visible to the citizen (notification). Do not include generic 'Retrieve Report' unless it is specifically contextualized for the rejection review context, but prioritize the core rejection actions.

high_level_goal.name: Manage the lifecycle of accepted reports
high_level_goal.description: Technical Office Staff should be able to track and update the status of accepted reports through various stages, from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved', ensuring efficient issue resolution.

actor.name: Technical Office Staff
actor.description: Municipal personnel responsible for managing accepted reports, assigning them, and updating their resolution status.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Manage the lifecycle of accepted reports' for the 'Technical Office Staff' actor. 

1. **Relevance**: All LLGs are directly related to tracking, assigning, updating status, and documenting reports, which aligns with the HLG description and the project documentation (Section B: Report Lifecycle).
2. **Consistency**: 
   - `llg_001` to `llg_003` cover retrieval and filtering, essential for tracking.
   - `llg_004` and `llg_005` cover assignment to external and internal parties, respectively, matching the documentation's distinction between Case 1 and internal handling.
   - `llg_006` and `llg_007` cover specific status transitions ('Work in Progress', 'Suspended') explicitly mentioned in the documentation.
   - `llg_008` and `llg_009` distinguish between manual resolution for external companies without access (Case 2) and standard resolution. While `llg_009` could potentially encompass `llg_008`, keeping them separate is not 'misleading' or 'duplicated' in a harmful way; it clarifies the specific workflow for external non-access cases. The documentation explicitly describes the manual move for Case 2, so having a specific LLG for it is supported.
   - `llg_010` covers internal comments, which the documentation states are visible to staff and external workers but not citizens. This is a valid part of managing the lifecycle (communication/documentation).
3. **Missing Capabilities**: The HLG focuses on the lifecycle from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved'. The initial transition from 'Pending Approval' to 'In Progress' is typically done by the Organization Office (approval), but the Technical Office takes over *after* approval. The LLGs start from retrieving *accepted* reports, which is correct. There is no obvious missing essential capability for the *Technical Office Staff* within the scope of *managing the lifecycle of accepted reports*. The assignment happens after approval, and the LLGs cover that. The transition to 'In Progress' is implied by the assignment or the start of work, but `llg_006` covers 'Work in Progress'. The documentation says: 'After approval, accepted reports move to the "In Progress" state... Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to "Work in Progress"'. The LLGs cover the states the Technical Office actively manages/updates. 

No LLGs are unsupported, misleading, duplicated in a conflicting way, or unrelated. The set is conservative and accurate.

branch_002.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Provide citizens with updates on their reports' is well-supported by the project description, specifically Section C (Citizen Updates), which details notifications, emails, and messaging for status changes and operator messages. The scope is correctly limited to the citizen's own reports, distinguishing it from the separate goal 'Enable citizens to follow public reports' (which covers other citizens' reports). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable citizens to effectively monitor and engage with reports' is broader and potentially overlaps with the 'follow public reports' goal, whereas the original goal is more precise and faithful to the specific functional intention of receiving updates on one's own submissions. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Provide citizens with updates on their reports'. The LLGs address: 1) Notifications for status changes (push, email, in-app) for own reports (llg_001-002, llg_005); 2) Notifications for new messages (push, email, in-app) for own reports (llg_003-004, llg_006); 3) The ability to reply to messages (llg_007); 4) Retrieval of own reports and details (llg_008-009); 5) Viewing public reports with filtering/sorting (llg_010-017); and 6) Following other citizens' reports and receiving updates for them (llg_018-023). 

While the HLG description focuses on 'their submitted reports', the documentation (Section C) explicitly states that citizens can 'follow other citizens' open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports)'. The inclusion of LLGs for following public reports (llg_018-023) is therefore supported by the documentation and falls within the scope of 'updates on reports' from the citizen's perspective. The sibling HLG 'Enable citizens to follow public reports' likely covers the *action* of following, but the *receipt of updates* for those followed reports is a distinct capability that aligns with the parent HLG's goal of providing updates. Even if there is slight overlap with the sibling HLG, the current LLGs are not contradicted by the documentation and cover all essential notification and retrieval capabilities described in Section C. No essential capability is missing, and no LLG is unsupported or misleading.

branch_004.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to follow public reports' is supported by the project description, specifically Section C ('CITIZEN UPDATES'), which states: 'Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens' open reports and receive notifications'. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Citizens to discover, view, and monitor the progress of public reports' accurately captures the functional intent derived from the low-level goals (finding, browsing, filtering, viewing details, subscribing, and receiving notifications). The original goal is reasonably scoped and distinct from 'Provide citizens with updates on their reports' (which focuses on the citizen's *own* reports) and 'Provide public visibility of urban issues' (which focuses on non-registered users). Therefore, the original goal should be kept as it faithfully represents the stakeholder intention. The current low-level goals (llg_001 to llg_009) comprehensively cover the capabilities required by the parent HLG 'Enable citizens to follow public reports'. 

1. **Discovery and Browsing**: llg_001 (retrieve list), llg_002 (filter by status), llg_003 (search by keyword), and llg_004 (retrieve details) allow citizens to find and understand public reports. This aligns with the documentation stating that accepted reports are visible on a map and in a summary table with filtering/sorting capabilities. Although the documentation mentions filtering by category and date as well, 'filter by status' is explicitly included, and 'search by keyword' covers general discovery. The absence of explicit 'filter by category' or 'filter by date' LLGs is not a material defect because these are standard variations of the filtering capability already represented by llg_002, and the core intent of narrowing down reports is satisfied. Furthermore, the sibling HLG 'Provide public visibility of urban issues' covers the general public view, but the current HLG focuses on the *citizen's* ability to follow, which implies active engagement (subscribing) and detailed tracking, which is well-covered.

2. **Following and Monitoring**: llg_005 (subscribe), llg_006 (unsubscribe), and llg_007 (list followed reports) directly address the 'follow' aspect mentioned in the documentation ('citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports'). 

3. **Notifications**: llg_008 (send notification) and llg_009 (view notifications) cover the mechanism by which citizens are informed of changes to followed reports. The documentation states that citizens receive notifications on the platform and via email (if enabled) for followed reports. llg_008 covers the system action of sending, and llg_009 covers the citizen's ability to view them. 

There are no contradictions with the documentation. The capabilities are atomic and API-mappable. No essential capability explicitly required by the parent HLG is absent. The sibling HLGs handle submission, anonymity, internal management, and general public viewing (non-registered), which are distinct from the citizen's active following/monitoring workflow.

branch_005.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate preliminary review of citizen reports' is well-supported by the project description, which explicitly states that the Organization Office performs a preliminary review to mark reports as accepted or rejected. The scope is appropriate for the actor. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Preliminary Review of Citizen Reports' is semantically equivalent but slightly more operational. The original goal's description ('efficiently review, accept, or reject... to ensure their validity') captures the intent well. There is no other HLG for this actor that covers the general review process (the other HLG for this actor, 'Ensure clear communication for rejected reports', is a specific sub-task/constraint of the rejection process, not the overall review goal). Therefore, the original goal is valid and should be kept. The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential workflow for the Organization Office Staff to conduct a preliminary review. 
1. **Identification**: LLG_001 allows staff to retrieve the list of pending reports.
2. **Information Gathering**: LLG_002 and LLG_003 allow staff to view detailed report information and attached media, which is necessary to assess validity and appropriateness.
3. **Decision Making**: LLG_004 covers accepting reports (moving to 'In Progress'), and LLG_005 covers rejecting reports (moving to 'Rejected' with a mandatory reason).

branch_009.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate internal communication on reports' is supported by the project description, specifically Section B (Case 1), which states that 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen'. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Private Communication on Reports' accurately captures the intent of the low-level goals (submitting and viewing private comments). The original goal's description ('exchange private comments and information with external maintenance personnel') is faithful to the documentation. While the name 'Facilitate internal communication' might be slightly ambiguous (as it involves external parties), the description clarifies the scope. The reconstructed goal 'Manage Private Communication on Reports' is arguably more precise regarding the 'private' nature and the 'management' aspect (viewing + submitting), but the original goal is not incorrect, generic, or unsupported. It represents a distinct functional intention from 'Manage the lifecycle' or 'Assign reports'. Therefore, it should be kept, as it correctly identifies the communication capability required for the Technical Office Staff. The parent HLG 'Facilitate internal communication on reports' requires Technical Office Staff to exchange private comments and information with external maintenance personnel. The current LLGs cover the two fundamental atomic capabilities for this interaction from the Technical Office Staff's perspective: submitting new comments (llg_001) and retrieving/viewing existing comments (llg_002). The documentation states that staff and external workers can 'exchange information and comments'. This exchange is composed of writing (submitting) and reading (retrieving) messages. The capability for external workers to submit comments is covered by the sibling HLG 'Facilitate communication with technical office staff'. The capability for external workers to view comments is implicitly part of their interaction or covered by their own HLGs, but from the perspective of the Technical Office Staff, they need to be able to see what the external workers have said (covered by llg_002) and say what they want (covered by llg_001). There are no other essential capabilities explicitly required for the Technical Office Staff in this specific HLG that are missing. branch_011.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Facilitate communication with technical office staff' is supported by the project description, which states that 'Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report'. However, there is a significant semantic overlap with the existing High-Level Goal 'Facilitate internal communication on reports' assigned to the 'Technical Office Staff'. This existing goal describes the same functional intention from the perspective of the Technical Office Staff ('exchange private comments and information with external maintenance personnel'). In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, a single interaction (communication) between two actors is typically modeled as one goal or a pair of strictly complementary goals. Having two separate high-level goals for the same bidirectional communication channel (one for each actor) creates redundancy. The existing goal for Technical Office Staff already covers the communication aspect. The other goal for External Maintenance Workers, 'Enable external personnel to manage assigned reports', covers the status update aspect. Therefore, the communication aspect for the External Maintenance Worker is already covered by the system's communication mechanism described in the Technical Office Staff's goal. To avoid splitting one stakeholder intention (or one system function) into wording variants for different actors, this goal should be removed as it is semantically covered by the existing 'Facilitate internal communication on reports' goal.

branch_012.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Configure automatic report assignments' is supported by the project description, specifically the note in Section B stating that automatic assignment of reports in certain categories to external companies is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Automatic Report Assignment Rules' suggests a broader scope (lifecycle management: create, modify, activate, deactivate, delete, view). While the original goal uses the verb 'Configure', which is reasonably accurate for setting up rules, the reconstruction highlights that the administrator needs full control over the lifecycle of these rules, not just initial configuration. However, 'Configure' is often used broadly in requirements to encompass the management of settings. Looking at the other HLGs, there is no other HLG for the Municipal Administrator covering this specific functional area (the other one is 'Access comprehensive system statistics'). The original goal is not generic, narrow, or incorrectly scoped. It captures the core intention: enabling the administrator to set up the logic for automatic assignment. The difference between 'Configure' and 'Manage' is minor and does not warrant a rewrite unless 'Configure' implies a one-time action, which is not strictly true in software contexts (configuration can be updated). However, the evaluator rationale notes that the LLGs describe 'creation, modification, activation, deactivation, deletion, and viewing'. 'Configure' might be seen as slightly narrow if it implies only initial setup. But typically, 'Configure X' allows for changing X. Let's look at the calibration: 'Generic, narrow... -> REWRITE'. Is 'Configure' too narrow? It covers the setup. The reconstruction 'Manage... Rules' is more precise regarding the lifecycle. However, the original description says 'configure the system to automatically assign...'. This is a valid functional intention. Is it less faithful than the reconstruction? The reconstruction is 'Manage Automatic Report Assignment Rules'. The original is 'Configure automatic report assignments'. The project description says 'previously configured by the municipal administrator'. The term 'configured' is used in the source text. Therefore, the original goal is faithful to the source text's terminology. The LLGs expand on what 'configure' entails (CRUD operations on the rules). Keeping the original is justified as it aligns with the source text's language and the actor's description ('Manages system configurations, such as automatic assignments'). The parent HLG 'Configure automatic report assignments' requires the Municipal Administrator to define, manage, and control the logic for automatically assigning reports of specific categories to external companies. The current LLGs cover the full lifecycle of these rules: retrieving necessary reference data (categories, companies), creating new rules, updating existing ones, activating/deactivating them (lifecycle management), deleting them, and viewing the current configuration. This decomposition is complete, atomic, and directly supports the parent intention. There are no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG that are absent from the LLGs. The LLGs do not contradict the documentation; the documentation confirms that such configuration is possible and managed by the municipal administrator. No capabilities from sibling HLGs (like manual assignment by Technical Office Staff) are incorrectly included.

branch_014.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Provide public visibility of urban issues' is supported by the project description, specifically Section C (Citizen Updates) and Section D (Statistics). The description explicitly states that accepted reports become visible on the portal for non-registered users via an interactive map and a summary table. The bottom-up reconstruction suggests a broader scope ('comprehensive access to urban issue report data and statistics'), but the existing HLG 'Display public statistics on urban issues' already covers the statistics aspect for the Public Viewer. 2. **Table View**: LLG_004 (retrieve paginated list), LLG_005 (filter list), LLG_006 (sort list), and LLG_007 (details from table) cover the summary table requirements, including filtering and sorting by category, status, or date as specified in Section C.

actor.name: Technical Office Staff
actor.description: Municipal personnel responsible for managing accepted reports, assigning them, and updating their resolution status.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description's functional requirements are fully covered by the existing High-Level Goals. Citizen registration and profile management (Section A, C) are standard prerequisites or sub-tasks of the 'Enable citizens to report urban inconveniences' and 'Provide citizens with updates' goals. The report lifecycle management (Section B) is covered by goals for Organization Office review, Technical Office lifecycle management, assignment, and external worker resolution. Communication channels (Section C) are covered by 'Provide citizens with updates' and 'Facilitate internal communication'. Public visibility and statistics (Section C, D) are covered by 'Provide public visibility of urban issues' and 'Display public statistics'. No distinct, undocumented functional intention exists that is not already addressed by the current HLG list.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Citizens to Report and Manage Urban Inconveniences
branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete lifecycle of a citizen's interaction with a system designed for addressing urban inconveniences. They cover the initial steps of user account creation and authentication, the detailed process of submitting a new urban inconvenience report with all necessary information and evidence, and the subsequent capabilities for citizens to track the status of their submitted reports, receive updates, and engage in communication with public administration regarding these reports.

branch_006.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Rejection of Citizen Reports with Justification
branch_006.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe a complete workflow for the Organization Office Staff to reject a citizen report. They cover initiating the rejection process, providing a mandatory explanation for the rejection, and finally, finalizing the rejection and notifying the citizen. All operations are integral steps in ensuring that report rejections are justified, documented, and properly communicated.

branch_007.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Resolution Status of Accepted Citizen Reports
branch_007.rationale: The low-level goals collectively enable the Technical Office Staff to comprehensively manage and monitor the resolution process for accepted citizen reports. They cover retrieving current status, updating status, querying reports based on status, and auditing the history of status changes, all of which are integral to overseeing the progress and completion of report resolutions.

branch_008.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Technical Office Staff to Assign and Prepare In Progress Reports for Work
branch_008.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe a complete workflow for the Technical Office Staff. This workflow starts with identifying unassigned 'In Progress' reports, proceeds through gathering details and selecting an appropriate responsible party and individual user, performs the actual assignment, and concludes with preparing the report for the assigned party to commence work by adding instructions and updating its status. All these steps are essential for moving a report from an unassigned 'In Progress' state to an assigned 'Work in Progress' state, ready for resolution.

branch_001.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Enable citizens to report urban inconveniences' is well-supported by the project description (Section A: REPORTS). The description explicitly details the process of submitting reports with specific fields (location, title, description, category, photos). The bottom-up reconstruction suggests 'Report and Manage', but 'Manage' is too broad for this specific HLG as it overlaps with other goals like 'Provide citizens with updates on their reports' and 'Allow citizens to control report anonymity'. The original goal is correctly scoped to the submission action, which is the primary functional intention of the citizen in this context. The description in the original HLG accurately reflects the requirements (location, description, category, photos). Therefore, the original goal is kept as it is faithful, supported, and appropriately scoped without unnecessary overlap. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential capabilities required by the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Enable citizens to report urban inconveniences'. The decomposition includes the necessary preconditions (registration, email confirmation, authentication) and the core reporting workflow (selecting category, entering description, selecting location, uploading photos, setting anonymity, and submitting the report). It also includes post-submission capabilities for the citizen to view their own reports and details, which are implicitly required for a complete interaction lifecycle. While the HLG description focuses on 'submitting', the actor description mentions 'receive updates', and the provided LLGs include notification and messaging capabilities (llg_012, llg_013, llg_014). Although these specific update/messaging capabilities might arguably belong to the sibling HLG 'Provide citizens with updates on their reports', their presence here does not constitute a material defect in the decomposition of the reporting HLG, as they are closely tied to the report lifecycle and do not contradict the documentation. The absence of a specific 'Edit Report' or 'Delete Report' capability is not a material defect as the documentation does not explicitly state that citizens can edit or delete reports after submission (only that they can submit and track). The granularity is appropriate, and no essential capability explicitly required by the parent HLG is missing. Therefore, the LLGs are kept.
